rated_messages.input_message: Think about a happy memory to ease the difficulty of your urge. Is there something you have been wanting to do for a while that you know you would enjoy? Reading? Walking? Calling a friend? Doing a puzzle? Do something that matters to you instead of smoking.
Whenever you think about smoking, listen to your favorite song and sing it out loud!
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
If this situation becomes stressful for you, make an excuse to leave for a few minutes. If this doesn't help, it might be better to just leave early.
Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
If you are tempted to smoke by being in this location, see if you can sit with that temptation for 1 minute. When the minute is over, do it again. Soon, it should pass.

You don't have to act on this feeling by smoking or doing anything about it. Give it some space, breathe, and see if it changes. Let the urge and feeling be there while you focus on doing something you care about.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
